universe.name: مرصد الإسناد · Isnād Observatory
universe.one_line: A computational universe for reading the Qur'an through الإسناد — grammatical attribution — and for finding the places where the attribution moves.
universe.language_of_record: Arabic. There are no translations in the application, by design. Code comments and this فهرس are bilingual.
universe.epistemic_stance: Everything the engine surfaces is استنباط آلي — computational extraction from morphological tagging. It points at where to look. It does not interpret, and it is not tafsīr. Any exposition served over this protocol inherits that stance and must not launder a structural finding into a claim about meaning.
universe.master_metric: lexicalContinuity × isnādDelta — maximum grammatical motion held against maximum lexical continuity. It fell out of three passages (هود ٢٩، ق ٢، القصص ٤-٥) rather than being imposed on them.
universe.runs_on: a fresh clone with no network, no database and no configuration: /data is committed.

invariants.rule: Every word's isnād spine must be resolved before anything aggregates over it. Āyah vectors, signatures, proximity distance and dominant person are all functions of the spine.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: Computing them in the same pass reads person: null for every word and silently yields 6,236 empty signatures — the whole mined layer becomes vacuous while every test still passes. This shipped once and was caught.

invariants.rule: A person tag is not attribution. Only verb-subject, subject-enclitic, detached and nasikh-subject seat a referent in the chair; object, possessive, prepositional and vocative merely point at one.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: رَبِّهِمْ would count as predicating to a third person, and every downstream metric would measure reference density instead of attribution.

invariants.rule: المخاطب sits at 0, المتكلم at 0.5, الغائب at 1. Direct address is the nearest a discourse can stand.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: It is not a person ordering; it is a discourse-distance ordering. Re-sorting it as 1-2-3 inverts the cosmos radius, the resonance distance term, and every reading of 'flying inward'.

invariants.rule: هود ٢٩، ق ٢، القصص ٤-٥ are the standard the engine is held to. npm run verify pins all three. If a change stops finding them, the change is wrong.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: The detectors were derived from these passages. Losing them means the tuning drifted off the thing it was tuned to.

invariants.rule: Detectors report structural configurations present in the morphology. None of them interpret, and the engine's prose never becomes tafsīr.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: The project's entire claim to honesty. Where a reading is the author's it is rendered in a distinct register labelled قراءة المؤلِّف, never as a finding.

invariants.rule: The application is Arabic only. No translations anywhere, by design.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: A translation would silently become the object of study in place of the text.

invariants.rule: /data holds only the raw corpus and the globally-mined indices. Spines, seams, frames and discoveries are rebuilt on request — ~80 ms for al-Baqarah — then cached.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: Pre-baking them took /data from 11 MB to 48 MB and froze detector thresholds that are supposed to be tunable per request.

invariants.rule: A composition stores loci and framing, never rendered text. The āyah, its words and its isnād are fetched from the corpus at watch time.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: The player's controls are controls of the text — السِّراج burns the isnād, القمر holds the paired āyah. Freeze the text and they become controls of a timeline.

invariants.rule: A declared lemma that matches nothing fails the build rather than passing silently.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: كُلَّمَا once matched zero occurrences: Arabic diacritics have no canonical order and the declared string ordered fatḥa before shadda where the corpus does the reverse. Nothing complained.

invariants.rule: Composition ids arrive from the URL and are used as filenames, so they must never be able to escape the directory.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: Path traversal on every file-backed deployment.

invariants.rule: The studio runs fully without Supabase: notes fall back to localStorage, compositions to JSON files, and the UI badge says which backend is live.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: A fresh clone would stop working, which is the property the whole /data commitment exists to protect.

invariants.rule: Detector thresholds are read from the query string and clamped at the server boundary, not baked into the data.
invariants.cost_of_breaking: Tuning would require a re-ingest, and no reader could ask the corpus a slightly different question.

discovery_kinds.gloss: The eight. Each reports a structural configuration; none interpret.

isnad_roles.gloss: The grammatical office a person-bearing segment holds. The first four seat a referent; the last four only point.

modules.role: Quotation frames, which the corpus does not mark — the system's largest declared heuristic.
modules.says: Quotation frames and the nested attribution tree. A frame opens at a verb of saying. Whether a later verb of saying *nests* inside it or *replaces* it is the whole difference between a dialogue and a speech-within-a-speech, and the corpus marks no quotation boundaries at all. The rule used here reads the verb's own inflection: A third-person verb (قَالَ، قَالُوا، يَقُولُ) is the narrator reporting, and an imperative (قُلْ) is the narrator commanding the addressee to speak. Both are narrator-leve

Signatures are compared, not words. 2. The chamber walk - a weighted graph over the whole muṣḥaf whose edges are the ʿarabī operations themselves (a shared motif, an inverted contour, a returning root, a bridge into the present, creation taking the chair). The walk is forbidden from using the same operation twice in a row,

modules.role: A suffix automaton over the whole muṣḥaf as one 23,784-symbol string.
modules.says: المثاني — mining repeated isnād contours with a suffix automaton. Each spine word contributes one symbol (person × tense), so the whole muṣḥaf becomes a single string over a twelve-letter alphabet. A suffix automaton over that string yields every right-maximal repeated contour at once, with no ceiling on length — which is the point: the interesting مثاني are not the ones we thought to look for.

exports.doc: Mine right-maximal repeated contours. A contour is right-maximal when no single-symbol extension preserves its occurrence count — i.e. it is the longest form of its own repetition, not an arbitrary window inside one.

modules.role: A whole sūrah as a composition, one strongest annotation per āyah.

modules.role: The attribution model itself: roles, weights, the proximity axis, seams, contours, signatures.
modules.says: الإسناد — deriving the musnad ilayh from morphology A person tag alone is not إسناد. `رَبِّهِمْ` references a 3rd person; it does not predicate to one. This module separates the segments that seat a referent in the attribution chair (SUBJECT_ROLES) from those that merely point at one — and that distinction is what every downstream detector stands on.
teaches: seating versus referencing
the contour alphabet
the 1↔3 inversion

exports.name: QAWL_ROOTS
exports.doc: Verbs of saying — these open a quotation frame.

exports.name: assignRoles
exports.doc: Assign a grammatical office to every person-bearing segment of one word. Mutates `segments` in place and returns the word's isnād spine.

exports.name: collectRefs
exports.doc: Every person a word touches, in any office.

exports.name: DISTANCE_OF
exports.doc: ── محور القرب والبُعد — the proximity axis المخاطب sits at zero: direct address is the nearest a discourse can stand. المتكلم sits mid: the speaker is present and witnessing but not addressed. الغائب sits far: reality narrated as structure, with no one in the room.

exports.name: roleWeight
exports.doc: Subject offices carry full weight; mere reference carries partial weight.

exports.name: personVector
exports.doc: Weighted person profile for a span of words. Uses every reference, not just spines: `أَرَىٰكُمْ` is 1st person predicated but unmistakably proximate, and a distance metric that ignored the كم would misread it.

exports.name: findSeams
exports.doc: Walk the spine-bearing words and record every turn. Words with no spine are transparent — الالتفات is measured between attributions, not between tokens.

exports.name: invertContour
exports.doc: The 1↔3 inversion of a contour: المتكلم and الغائب trade seats.

exports.name: signature
exports.doc: Compressed per-ayah person signature, e.g. "3312".

modules.role: The الاستعاذة entrance: six phases, its plates, and the final reveal.
modules.says: الاستعاذة — the entry sequence into the Immersive Qur'an. Structure, not prose. Each plate names a عَلَم and the engine resolves its closed set live, so no count in this file can ever drift from the corpus: the plate says "ثلاثة مواضع" only because the index returned three. Two registers are kept strictly apart and are styled differently wherever they are rendered: evidence what the morphology shows. Checkable. Not an opinion. reading the composer's reading of it. Marked as his, never as a findi
teaches: counts never written into copy — they come from the live index

exports.name: KHAL3
exports.doc: The خلع check. Written to what the sources actually say: neither text names him. The ḥadīth (al-Bukhārī 3124, Muslim 1747) says `نَبِيٌّ مِنَ الأَنْبِيَاءِ`, and 18:60 says `فَتَاهُ`. The identification as Yūshaʿ b. Nūn is commentary. Withholding the name is the point being made here, so overstating

exports.name: NUJUM
exports.doc: The final reveal, after the plates.

exports.name: ISTIADHA_KEY

modules.says: المعاجم — closed lexicons the detectors reason over. Keyed on the corpus LEMMA (normalised in this fork), because many entities share a root with unrelated words: نار and نور both sit under ROOT:نور.
teaches: where the engine knowingly stops being general

exports.name: KHALQ_LEMMAS
exports.doc: ألسنة الخلق — creation that the Qur'an seats in the isnād chair.

exports.name: AGENCY_ROOTS
exports.doc: Roots that predicate an *act* to their subject — speech, praise, witness, submission, refusal, motion. When one of these takes a خلق subject, that creature is not being described; it is doing something.

exports.name: RUSUL_LEMMAS
exports.doc: أنباء الرسل — messenger names as they lemmatise in the corpus.

exports.name: QASAS_ACTORS
exports.doc: Antagonists and nations — the other pole of the قصص.

exports.name: ZAMAN_LEMMAS
exports.doc: Lemmas that name time itself. Density of these is what lets a قصة declare its own clock — and what makes a shift into the imperfect land as *now*.

exports.name: LABTH_ROOTS
exports.doc: لبث — the verb Al-Kahf uses to suspend and then audit elapsed time.

the FAM: token that identifies a نسخ family

exports.name: parseFeatures
exports.doc: The first non key:value token is the segment's primary tag. Where the corpus gives none (a bare verb stem) we fall back to the tense, then the class.

exports.name: particleFamily

modules.role: Twelve time modalities and the before↔after axis they sit on.
modules.says: وحدة الزمن — the time modalities, and how an āyah is read for them. Not a taxonomy imposed on the text. Every modality below is anchored to particles the corpus actually tags, with the counts they actually have, so the flight board is programming real material rather than a metaphor: إِذ 309 · إِذا 383 · لَمّا 154 · قَد 406 · لَن 106 · لَم 348 لَو 189 · إِن 578 · لَوْلا 34 · س 119 · سَوْف 42 · أَبَدًا 28 · كُلَّما 15 The point of the module is that these are not all "time" in one sense. لَن fore
teaches: that time here is not one axis
tension as how much an āyah does with time

exports.name: TimeVector
exports.doc: Counts per modality, in MODALITIES order.

exports.name: timeVectorOf
exports.doc: Read one āyah's segments for every modality at once.

exports.name: timeAxisOf
exports.doc: Where an āyah sits on before↔after: each modality pulls toward its own axis position, weighted by how many times it fires. An āyah with no time marking at all sits at zero rather than being forced onto the line.

exports.name: timeTensionOf
exports.doc: How much an āyah *does* with time, as opposed to merely being in it. High where distinct modalities co-occur — a past that carries a counterfactual that carries a foreclosed future.

exports.name: TimeRoute
exports.doc: A programmed route through modalities — the FMC's legs.

exports.name: satisfies
exports.doc: Does an āyah satisfy a leg?
